# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-27 (Extended v186)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to autumn Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures was forged. **Kassa Brackick whispered that Islan Thornmere had secretly married Yera Haskick, but nobody could say where or when (autumn Year 7—NEW)**.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek Prydenridge gave up being a miller and took work as a brewer (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle Lindmere found work in Elmhaven, moved there (summer Year 7). Marald Corrford followed to Elmhaven within month (summer Year 7). Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew and became ferryman (summer Year 7).

**Solemn promises**: Elra Corrford gave Matho Stenson solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work (carry sealed letter to Torton) never begun.

## Spring/Summer/Autumn Year 7 Observations

Residents walked long way to avoid muddy square. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall (repeated observations, present in autumn Year 7). Multiple residents hummed childhood tunes while scrubbing steps: Yera, Rinelle, Zavus, Kadan, Bremira, Rorald Lindmere, Nerine, Lurald Stenworth. **Volan Stenworth and Kassa Brackick each counted coins twice, came up penny short (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. **Matho, Bremira, Thizek, and Pelia each counted coins twice, came up penny short**. **Matho Stenson, Thizek Stenenridge, and Volan Stenworth fell asleep in chair before fire had caught**. River remarks—multiple residents observed river up; others said it always was in spring: Taric/Kassa, Sebin/Rorald Lindmere, Elra/Fenelle Lindmere, Zavus/Bremira Corrford, Thizek/Isvie. Ismira asked if it would rain; Fenelle only shrugged. Ismira, Bremira, Ferald argued with carter over oat prices. Kadan and Rovus talked of weather, harvest, lame horse; discussed salt price scandal. Bremira and Ferald discussed salt price scandal. Yewyn and Pelia discussed salt price scandal. Fenelle and Ismira agreed "price of salt is scandal." Yera, Sebin, Pelia, Bremira, Thizek laughed at stories nobody else found funny. Yera and Zavus complained of aching backs. Pelia complained of aching back as usual. Luvie complained of aching back as usual (Ostcombe). Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. Children chased hoop down lane. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Yewyn, Tatho, Isvie Stenworth bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Yewyn appeared tired; Pelia noted this. Tatho, Bremira, Zavus, Fenelle Lindmere, Thizek Stenenridge, Yera Stenworth mended torn sleeve by window and said little (autumn Year 7). "Will it rain?" asked Tatho/Vesmira; Rorald/Isric Thornmere only shrugged. **"You look tired," Ilrald told Isric Thornmere, who did not deny it (autumn Year 7, Ostcombe—NEW)**. **"You look tired," Vesmira told Movie Prydenridge, who did not deny it (barricade period—NEW)**. Tatho and Istho Stenworth spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight (autumn Year 7). Baker's boy late again, line at oven grew long. **Lurald Stenworth read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. Zavus and Fenelle read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Wind came off water with smell of salt and tar. Rain threatened since morning but held off. **Nerine and Volan each watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. **Movie Prydenridge walked long way round to avoid muddy square (autumn Year 7, Ostcombe—NEW)**.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Discovery

**Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Upon arriving at Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Valjean understood Cosette was escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar. Into paternity his life's widowhood introduced all shades of love—daughter, mother, sister, woman, wife. Grief surpassed bounds; quiver of revolt ran head to foot; immense reawakening of egotism; the *I* howled. **Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Valjean at barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Took aim at fireman acting as sentinel on neighboring roof, smashed his helmet with bullet. When officer replaced sentinel, Valjean took aim again, sent officer's casque away. Officer retired speedily. No further attempts to spy on barricade made thereafter. Stared silently at wall opposite during barricade phase.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged she never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie. **During first phase**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Mental state (6th June, dawn)**: Fasting, fevered, emerged from all hope, plunged into visionary stupor. Felt he had entered tomb. **Marius recognizes Inspector (6th June)**: Upon seeing inspector of Rue de Pontoise striding over barricade to his death, Marius recalled inspector had handed him two pistols, which he used in this barricade.

**Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt thoroughly reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come. Back court surrounded by high walls. Burst into tears. Observed martin's nest in ancient cornice. Watched mother spread wings like fan over brood; father fluttered about bearing food. Hair in sunlight, soul absorbed in chimæras, gazed at birds with profound trouble virgin nest produces.

## Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie (24th June into 6th June)

**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and spiral staircase; cellar via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. Serving-maids: Matelote, Gibelotte. **Two barricades**: Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour. **Larger barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Height six or seven feet, stepped construction, paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole with ropes, red flag. Forty-three insurgents. **Three-front fortification**: Walled on Rue de la Chanvrerie (front), Rues du Cygne and de la Petite Truanderie (left), Rue Mondétour (right). Almost impregnable but fatally hemmed in. No exit.

**Enjolras's orders (6th June)**: Directed two-thirds of piled stones from Corinthe door carried to first floor and attic. Loop-holes carefully planned by Feuilly allowed gun-barrel passage. Ordered eight guns kept loaded, swords and pistols in belts. Twenty men to barricade. Six ambushed in attic windows and first-floor window. Upon drum beating assault, twenty below stairs to rush barricade.

**Key events**: Javert arrested, identified as Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two. Le Cabuc executed by Enjolras for killing. M. Mabeuf, aged eighty, tore flag from Enjolras, upheld red banner; died heroically; body lay in kitchen on table. Gavroche collected cartridges under heavy fire, finally struck by bullet, staggered, sank in sitting posture, raised both arms, sang. Éponine's corpse discovered after crossing barrier—livid face, streaming hair, pierced hand, half-nude breast. Corpses formed terrible pile nearby.

**Two lost children in Luxembourg Garden (6th June, daytime)**: One aged seven, one aged five, pale and ragged. Elder broke brioche into two portions, took small one for himself, gave large one to brother.

**Philosophical reflections on revolution and progress**: Revolutionists accused of sowing fear; their theories incriminated; aim suspected. Barricades seem crimes but combatants worthy of veneration—failure possesses majesty; martyrdom preferred to success. John Brown greater than Washington; Pisacane greater than Garibaldi. These men perform religious acts in obedience to divine stage-manager; French Revolution is act of God. Insurrection aims at ideal alone, not merely government or regime. 1832 chiefs combated not Louis Philippe precisely but usurpation of man over man, privilege over right in universe. Paris without king results in world without despots. Ideal distant, vague, retreats before efforts, but great. Revolutionists sacrifice themselves for visions often illusions, but illusions mingled with human certainty. Defend right, natural law, sovereignty of each one over himself. In worst case, die like three hundred Spartans. Poetry of people is element of progress; civilization measured by quantity of imagination. Modern ideal has type in art, means in science. Eden reconstructed by A+B. Races petrified in dogma or demoralized by lucre unfit to guide civilization. France Athenian in beauty, Roman in greatness; good, gives herself to sacrifice; subject to relapses into materialism. Peoples possess right to eclipse; all well provided light returns and eclipse does not degenerate into night.
